summary: This case study details the architectural refinement of macOS Space change detection and Mission Control reordering handling within the SuperDimmer menu-bar utility. It offers valuable, practical insights into combining NSWorkspace notifications with plist polling and undocumented SkyLight client APIs while resolving performance bottlenecks caused by redundant observers.
strengths: Addresses a concrete, real-world macOS systems programming challenge with actionable engineering patterns.
Provides clear code snippets demonstrating the integration of workspace notifications and CoreGraphics/SkyLight symbols.
Documents a tangible debugging narrative regarding CPU usage reduction and notification fan-out elimination.
Includes a comprehensive supporting repository file structure confirming the codebase authenticity.
weaknesses: Relies on undocumented CoreGraphics Services symbols which carry potential compatibility risks across minor macOS updates.
Post-fix CPU metrics are cited as design criteria rather than empirically captured traces.
Migration strategy for old integer-based visit histories carries minor edge cases if reorders occurred prior to upgrade.
suggestions: Incorporate actual Instruments or Activity Monitor traces for pre- and post-singleton performance comparisons.
Document fallback behaviors explicitly should Apple alter the `com.apple.spaces.plist` schema in future macOS versions.

claims.text: macOS posts NSWorkspace.activeSpaceDidChangeNotification on a Space switch but does not identify which Space became active
CGSMainConnectionID and CGSGetActiveSpace are undocumented CoreGraphics Services functions used by window management utilities
SuperDimmer uses ~/Library/Preferences/com.apple.spaces.plist to determine space identifiers and display order
claims.source: Supporting repository documentation and code references
